replies.What is your relationship with mathemati: I don't have a great relationship with maths. It's one of my least favorite subjects because it feels abstract and hard to grasp sometimes. I prefer more practical or visual subjects like biology, which makes more sense to me.
replies.Do you ever get anxious when thinking ab: Yes, I do feel anxious when thinking about maths. The complexity and the fear of making mistakes make me stressed. It's not something I enjoy, so it adds to my anxiety.
replies.Did you ever use AI to support your math: No, I haven't used AI for math learning. I mostly rely on textbooks and teachers. Maybe if I had tried AI, it could have helped me understand better, but I'm not sure.
replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: First, write the equation in standard form: ax² + bx + c = 0. Then, calculate the discriminant (Δ = b² -4ac). If Δ > 0, there are two real roots; if Δ=0, one root; if Δ<0, no real roots. Finally, use the quadratic formula x = [-b ± √(b²-4ac)] / 2a to find the roots.

To find stationary points, first take the derivative of f(x) with respect to x. Set the derivative equal to zero and solve for x. These solutions are the x-values of the stationary points. To determine if they're maxima or minima, use the second derivative test.
